subject: Residency & Subprocessor routing assessment for Medivault onboarding
messages:
From: Lauren Barton <lauren.barton@medivault.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medivault.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Residency and subprocessor routing — Medivault onboarding

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profiles. Legal has a couple of follow-ups before we move to a pilot:

1) We need to understand how Redwood would merge a HIPAA BAA request with GLBA obligations for our financial-ops subservice (we run payment facilitation for clinical billing). Can you outline approach to a combined addendum or routing rules?
2) Residency: we need a clear fallback if US-only residency is required for a workload (can certain calls be routed to US-only Dedicated nodes?).
3) Subprocessors: provide a list and whether any third-party analytics/KMS partners are outside the US.

Attached is our short DPA questionnaire (Medivault_DPA_Questionnaire.pdf) — Ellen (cc) is our counsel and will drive contractual redlines.

Timing: procurement is aiming for answers and evidence within two weeks (by 9/13). Is that feasible?

Best,
Lauren Barton
Head of Platform Partnerships
Medivault Inc.

--- Attachment: Medivault_DPA_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Barton <lauren.barton@medivault.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ellen Price <ellen.price@stantonlegal.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessor routing — Medivault onboarding

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear list. Short summary and next steps below.

Summary answers:
- Combined obligations: Redwood supports a layered approach rather than a single monolithic addendum. For HIPAA-covered PHI we offer a BAA; for GLBA-scoped data we can append a GLBA exhibit. Operationally, we implement routing policies so requests flagged as GLBA-only traffic are steered to Dedicated pools with the appropriate residency and encryption controls.
- Residency fallbacks: yes — we can configure a US-only Dedicated region (Dedicated or Private) and an automatic routing policy that fails over to it when a workload flag is set. That is an enterprise-configured option and will require Reserved capacity if you need sustained throughput.
- Subprocessors: current list below (summary). Full vendor list and locations will be provided in the evidence folder.

Immediate ask: Marcus and Soojin will own the technical feasibility write-up + evidence pack. Marcus — can you produce a short runbook for the routing policy and capacity impact? Soojin — can you compile the subprocessor inventory and residency status (highlight non-US vendors)?

Timeline suggestion: 9/13 for initial answers + evidence links, 9/20 for any contract redline sync with Ellen. If you need faster, propose a 9/8 working session.

Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessor routing — Medivault onboarding

Thanks — jumping in with technical notes. Sketch below is draft for the runbook we'll hand to Medivault:

1) Data classification trigger points
- Request-level header tag (x-mv-data-class) set by Medivault client or via token scoping
- Prompt-level metadata flag for PHI/GLBA

2) Smart routing rules
- If x-mv-data-class == PHI -> route to Dedicated PHI pool (US region)
- If x-mv-data-class == GLBA -> route to Dedicated GLBA pool (US-only)
- Else -> hosted pool (global) with redaction/caching controls

3) Failover behavior
- If designated Dedicated capacity unavailable -> immediate 503 with optional auto-failover only if Medivault opts into cross-region fallback (policy-controlled)

4) Capacity impact (ballpark)
- Pilot: reserve 2x r5-gpu equivalent slots to meet 95th percentile throughput for your demo profile

I'll compile a one-page PDF and a capacity delta table. Also attaching an evidence template we can fill (Medivault_Evidence_Request_Template.xlsx).

-Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: Medivault_Evidence_Request_Template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Ellen Price <ellen.price@stantonlegal.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Barton <lauren.barton@medivault.com>
Cc: procurement@medivault.com, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessor routing — Medivault onboarding

Thanks — a few contractual and evidence asks from our side:

- We need confirmation that any KMS/HSM providers used for PHI key management are either US-headquartered or that key material remains under Medivault control. Please state which KMS partners may be in scope and whether Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK) is supported.
- For GLBA scope, we need an attestation on access controls (least privilege + separation between analytics and inference teams).
- Please provide a copy of your proposed BAA exhibit and any GLBA-specific language you plan to attach.

Also, can Redwood confirm log retention windows for requests flagged as PHI vs non-PHI? Medivault requires 1 year retention for PHI logs and 90 days for non-PHI operational logs.

Ellen Price
Counsel, Stanton Legal (on behalf of Medivault)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Price <ellen.price@stantonlegal.com>, Lauren Barton <lauren.barton@medivault.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessor routing — Medivault onboarding

Ellen/Lauren — thanks for the concrete asks. Short responses below; attaching links to the evidence folder in Drive and the draft BAA+GLBA exhibits for your review.

- KMS: Redwood supports BYOK and has integrations with AWS KMS (multi-region), Google Cloud KMS, and an HSM-backed partner for dedicated deployments. For PHI keys we recommend BYOK or Dedicated HSM so key material remains under customer control. Non-US KMS partners are not used for PHI key material by default — our current public-hosted control plane uses regional KMS services but PHI workflows are configurable to US-only KMS via Private/Dedicated deployment.

- Access controls/attestation: we will provide our internal role matrix and an attestation statement about separation of duties. For GLBA-scoped workloads we can include an additional constraint in the exhibit requiring separate service accounts and explicit ACLs.

- Log retention: we can support 1 year for PHI request logs and 90 days for non-PHI operational logs. We will document retention controls in the DPA exhibit and provide example retention scripts for evidence.

Next steps:
- Evidence folder (read-only link): https://drive.company/redwood/medivault/privacy-evidence
- Draft BAA+GLBA exhibits (DocuSign template): https://app.docusign.com/templates/Redwood-Medivault-BAA-GLBA
- Proposed timeline: final evidence and an editable draft of the exhibits by 2026-09-13; contract redline meeting w/ Ellen week of 9/20.

If helpful, Marcus and Soojin are available for a 30-min technical deep-dive next Wednesday (9/15).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
